Closed-form root of the directed layer

Source: R/dag_layer.R
mc_dag_closed_root.Rd

Solves the Pearson estimating equations of the modified Cholesky (LDL) layer of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) directly, from the covariance of the Pearson residuals. Because the structural matrix has unit determinant, the Gaussian working criterion of the residual layer separates by node, $$\ell^p_e=-\frac n2\sum_{j=1}^R\left\{\log\delta_j+ \frac{q_j(\boldsymbol\gamma_j)}{\delta_j}\right\},\qquad q_j=\widehat S_{e,jj}-2\boldsymbol\gamma_j^\top\widehat{\mathbf S}_{e,P_j,j} +\boldsymbol\gamma_j^\top\widehat{\mathbf S}_{e,P_jP_j}\boldsymbol\gamma_j,$$ so the system is \(R\) independent least-squares problems and its root is $$\hat{\boldsymbol\gamma}_j=\widehat{\mathbf S}_{e,P_jP_j}^{-1} \widehat{\mathbf S}_{e,P_j,j},\qquad \hat\delta_j=\widehat S_{e,jj}-\widehat{\mathbf S}_{e,j,P_j} \widehat{\mathbf S}_{e,P_jP_j}^{-1}\widehat{\mathbf S}_{e,P_j,j}.$$ For a fixed directed support the layer is therefore a sequence of least-squares regressions of the Pearson residuals of each response on those of its parents. A response with no parent keeps \(\hat\delta_j=\widehat S_{e,jj}\) and contributes no coefficient. Here \(P_j\) is the set of parents of response \(j\), \(\boldsymbol\gamma_j\) the vector of its coefficients \(\gamma_{jk}\), \(k \in P_j\), and \(n\) the number of units; the criterion is written up to an additive constant.

Usage

mc_dag_closed_root(Shat, R, edges = NULL, ordering = NULL, directed = FALSE)

Arguments

Shat

the \(R \times R\) covariance of the Pearson residuals, in the order of the responses.

R

a single positive integer, the number of responses.

edges

optional two-column integer matrix of response indices. With directed = FALSE each row is an unordered adjacency and its direction follows ordering (the earlier response is the parent). With directed = TRUE each row is an arc (parent, child); each pair of responses may appear at most once, and self-loops are refused. If NULL, the complete DAG on ordering is used.

ordering

optional integer permutation of 1:R giving the order of the responses in the factorization, parents before children, so that ordering[1] has no parent; NULL uses 1:R. With directed = TRUE it is derived from the arcs when left NULL, and checked against them when supplied.

directed

logical; TRUE reads the columns of edges as parent and child rather than as an unordered pair.

Value

A list with gamma, delta, the implied Sigma_b and K_b in the order of the responses, the edges actually used as (parent, child) pairs in response labels with gamma aligned to their rows, the ordering, the parents of each response, and status, which records how many nodes needed a ridge on their normal equations, how many innovation variances were lifted to the positivity floor (\(10^{-10}\widehat S_{e,jj}\)), and ill_conditioned, the responses whose parent block, rescaled to a unit diagonal, has a reciprocal condition number at or below .Machine$double.eps^(2/3); their coefficients are not identified and come from a solve with a ridge of \(10^{-8}\) on that unit diagonal. Both tests are invariant to a rescaling of the responses, and so is the root: rescaling response \(j\) by \(a_j\) multiplies \(\gamma_{jk}\) by \(a_j/a_k\) and \(\delta_j\) by \(a_j^2\). A nonzero status means the residual covariance is close to singular on some parent set, and mcglm_graph then does not certify the fit for inference. delta is indexed by response, like the diagonal of Sigma_b.

Relation to the iterative engine

mcglm_graph takes this route by default. Passing control = list(dag_solver = "newton") runs instead the scoring iteration on \((\boldsymbol\gamma,\log\boldsymbol\delta)\) that the directed and undirected layers share. It solves the same system and serves as an independent check on the closed form.

Giving the arcs directly

With directed = FALSE the edges are unordered adjacencies and their direction comes from ordering, as elsewhere in the package. That is awkward when the support to fit is an estimated DAG, whose arcs need not run along the natural order of the responses. With directed = TRUE the two columns of edges are read as parent and child, any acyclic set of arcs is accepted, and a compatible ordering is derived internally by Kahn's algorithm. A cyclic set is refused, since it has no modified Cholesky factorization at all.

References

Pourahmadi, M. (1999). Joint mean-covariance models with applications to longitudinal data: unconstrained parameterisation. Biometrika 86(3), 677-690. doi:10.1093/biomet/86.3.677

See also

mc_dag_sensitivity, mc_dag_coefficients

Other directed layer: mc_build_D_matrix(), mc_build_T_matrix(), mc_cholesky_derivatives(), mc_cholesky_to_covariance(), mc_cholesky_to_precision(), mc_dag_coefficients(), mc_dag_sensitivity(), mc_dag_unit_diagonal()

Examples

S <- mc_cholesky_to_covariance(c(0.7, 0.3, 0.5), c(1, 0.64, 0.49),
                               R = 3)$Sigma_b
fit <- mc_dag_closed_root(S, R = 3)
round(fit$gamma, 12)     # recovers the generating coefficients
#> [1] 0.7 0.3 0.5
round(fit$delta, 12)
#> [1] 1.00 0.64 0.49
